reason: Resiliency page: most administrative functions only from the primary Region, incl. external IdP connection, user/group sync, creating and assigning permission sets; applications and their assignments managed in the Region where created.
AWS managed applications page: assignments required by default; app administrator can choose; if required only users assigned directly or via group can view the tile.
Sessions page: application sessions (with AWS managed applications) default one hour lifetime, refreshed while the user interactive session is valid, end at next refresh typically within 30 minutes.
FAQ answers No to native mobile and desktop SSO: supports single sign-on to business applications through web browsers only.
Table under Designed for availability: data plane incl. sign-in 99.95%, control plane 99.90%, in a single Region; values are design goals, not an SLA.

Note: even if replicated, AWS recommends break-glass access for a small group of privileged users; emergency access uses external IdP identities instead of IAM users and does not protect against an IdP disruption.
Document history row dated April 17, 2025: can no longer provision AD users with IAM Identity Center AD Sync; use configurable AD Sync instead.
Document history row dated September 17, 2025: added support for customer managed KMS keys to encrypt workforce identity data at rest.
Document history row dated July 14, 2022, titled Support for permissions boundaries and customer managed policies in permission sets; description covers AWS managed and customer managed policies.

Document history row dated May 28, 2026: permission and application access changes from group membership now take effect immediately when creating new sessions; claim is framed as what the guide states.
Document history row dated August 4, 2026: choose whether to enable multi-account permissions when creating an organization instance; enabled by default; can be enabled later.
Document history row dated February 2, 2026: multi-Region support incl. replication to additional Regions, account access and AWS managed applications in additional Regions.
Document history row dated July 28, 2026: multi-Region support now works with the Identity Center directory as identity source, in addition to external IdPs.

Document history row dated August 6, 2026: Multi-Region option for new organization instances in supported Regions automatically creates a customer managed KMS key and replicates to an additional Region; condition kept in qualifiers.
Document history row dated July 26, 2022: AWS SSO renamed to AWS IAM Identity Center; features include application assignments, multi-account permissions and an AWS access portal.
Document history row dated June 22, 2026: separate quotas for AWS accounts and applications, previously one combined quota, new default 7,000 each.

Considerations page: changing identity source might remove all user and group assignments; then all users incl. the administrative user lose SSO access; the 'already managing users' condition is kept in qualifiers.
Important box: changing identity source type to or from AD changes the Identity Store ID, with the implication that the default AWS access portal URL will change.
Quotas page Note: recommend AWS CLI and APIs to centrally administer above 50,000 users, 10,000 groups, 500 permission sets or 3,000 applications; a recommendation, as qualified.
CLI integration page: v2 sign-in with same AD or Identity Center credentials, list and switch between assigned accounts and roles, CLI manages short-term credentials automatically; all three quoted.
Prerequisites page: use for AWS managed applications only, accounts only, or both; existing IAM federation for account access can continue while Identity Center serves application access.
FAQ: Cognito manages identities for customer facing applications and is not a supported identity source; workforce identities in Identity Center or external source such as AD, Okta, Entra ID.
Configurable AD sync page: explicitly configure which AD identities sync and control the sync process; context bullets list defining users/groups and pausing and resuming the sync.

Account access page: assign connected-directory users permissions to management or member accounts by common job functions or custom permissions; Identity Center configures the permissions automatically.
FAQ: control access to the Management Console and CLI v2 through single sign-on; the AWS Mobile Console app also supports IAM Identity Center.
FAQ: does not create IAM users and groups, has its own identity store; creates and manages IAM roles in individual accounts for each permission set granted.
FAQ: applications not in the pre-integrated list can be configured as a custom SAML 2.0 application if they support SAML 2.0; condition kept.

Policies page: Identity Center does not create customer managed policies; create them in advance in each account matching name and path; assignment fails if the policy does not exist in the member account.

Region data page: all configured data incl. directory configurations, permission sets, application instances and user assignments is stored in the Region where enabled; claim does not say 'only', so later replication does not contradict it.
Decision guide, Federation with IAM: federate workforce users through an IdP to specific accounts via OIDC or SAML 2.0; users assume IAM roles.
Decision guide table row: workforce access to accounts and resources -> IAM Identity Center or Federation with IAM; additional: Control Tower, centralized root access, temporary security credentials.
Identity source page: on first enable, automatically configured with Identity Center directory as default identity source unless a different source is chosen.
Delegated administration best practices: management-account permission sets can only be modified by an Identity Center admin from the management account; the delegated administrator can't alter them.
Delegated administration page: instance must always reside in the management account; administration can be delegated to a member account; benefit minimizes people needing management-account access.

SRA Org Management page: runs in the Org Management account by default; for least privilege administration can be delegated to a member account; in the SRA the Shared Services account is delegated admin.
Considerations bullet: users deleted or disabled using Identity Store APIs who have active sessions can continue to access integrated applications and accounts; scope and condition kept.

Revoke page: a disabled user with an active portal session can keep assuming new roles until access (the permission set assignments of that step) is removed; deleting the session removes portal access immediately.

Sessions table row User's access disabled: immediate loss of Identity Center access and new app sessions, existing app sessions within 30 minutes, account sessions within 12 hours or less per permission set session duration.
FAQ: does not modify any existing IAM roles, users or policies; creates new roles and policies for use through IAM Identity Center.

Emergency access page: users sign in to the console via direct (SAML 2.0, per context) federation with usual credentials; works when Identity Center is down but IAM data plane and IdP are up; deploy before a disruption.
